t: This is Lansdowne House, now numbered 9 Fitzmaurice Place, the surviving part of a grand aristocratic town house just south of Berkeley Square. Robert Adam designed it. It passed through a striking run of owners, and several of them were prime ministers: the Earl of Bute, who led the country from 1762 to 1763, then William Petty, Earl of Shelburne, who was prime minister at the end of the American War of Independence and made peace with America. William Pitt the Younger and Lord Rosebery are also named among its owners. So is Harry Gordon Selfridge, the founder of Selfridges.
